faqs.a: Subresource Integrity (SRI) lets a page verify that a fetched file (script, stylesheet) matches a cryptographic hash before executing it. If a CDN is compromised or serves a different file, the browser blocks it instead of running attacker's code.

SHA-384 is the current sweet spot: stronger than SHA-256 with negligible cost, and it's what most documentation and examples use. SHA-512 also works everywhere modern. SHA-256 is fine too — all three are supported by every modern browser.

No. The hash must be computed over the exact bytes served. Any change — even one character, a line-ending change, or different minification — produces a completely different hash and the browser will block the file. Recompute the hash every time the file changes.
faqs.q: Can I reuse a hash after updating the library?

faqs.a: Always include crossorigin="anonymous". Without it, the browser can't perform the integrity check on cross-origin resources properly, and the check may fail or be skipped. It's required for SRI to work with CDNs.

Because the browser compares against the exact bytes it downloads. Hash your local file, upload it unchanged, and reference the same file. Line-ending conversions (CRLF vs LF) or BOM changes during upload are classic causes of mismatch.
faqs.q: My hash doesn't match the file on the server — why?

faqs.a: Mostly no: SRI only verifies file integrity, not that the library is safe or bug-free. It protects against tampered CDNs and man-in-the-middle modification, which is exactly the threat it was designed for. Keep libraries updated regardless.
faqs.q: Does SRI protect against all supply-chain attacks?

sri-hash-generator.formula:
integrity = "sha256-" | "sha384-" | "sha512-"  +  base64( SHA(file bytes) )

<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js"
  integrity="sha384-<base64>"
  crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

The hash covers the EXACT bytes served — one changed byte invalidates it.

keyFacts: SRI (Subresource Integrity) is a browser feature that checks a file's hash before executing it.
The integrity attribute holds the algorithm plus the base64-encoded hash: sha384-<base64>.
Supported algorithms: sha256, sha384, sha512 — all work in every modern browser.
crossorigin="anonymous" is required for the check to run on cross-origin resources.
The hash must match the served bytes exactly — even whitespace changes invalidate it.
If the check fails, the browser blocks the resource and logs a console error — the page keeps working without it.

Input: the 5 characters hello (5 bytes), algorithm SHA-256.

3. Base64 of the digest: LPJNul+wow4m6DsqxbninhsWHlwfp0JecwQzYpOLmCQ=.
4. Integrity value: sha256-LPJNul+wow4m6DsqxbninhsWHlwfp0JecwQzYpOLmCQ=

<script src="https://cdn.example.com/library.js"
  integrity="sha256-LPJNul+wow4m6DsqxbninhsWHlwfp0JecwQzYpOLmCQ="
  crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
